title: security: rbac v2 enforce KMS region residency + audit logging hardening
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Enforce KMS region residency at RBAC v2 policy evaluation time and strengthen audit logging for KMS- and residency-related operations. Includes DB migration, backwards-compatible feature flag, tests, and docs update.
description: Context: Several customers and recent compliance reviews requested stricter enforcement of KMS region residency constraints alongside RBAC v2 policies and clearer audit trails for key operations (SUP-9843, ENG-4321). Motivation: previously we audited residency violations but allowed inconsistent enforcement across control planes; this PR hardens enforcement paths and ensures all relevant operations emit high-fidelity audit events. Summary of changes: 1) Policy enforcement: RBAC v2 policy evaluator now validates requested KMS key region against resource residency constraints during role/credential creation and runtime policy checks; enforcement occurs when the 'rbac.v2.kms_residency.enforce' feature flag is true. 2) Audit logging: all KMS-related operations (key_reference creation, rotation, assignment to resources, and policy evaluation denials) now include structured fields: kms_key_id, kms_region, policy_id, decision, and actor metadata. 3) Migration: added a lightweight migration to add kms_residency_policies table and backfill from existing resource tags; migration is transactional and idempotent. 4) Backwards compatibility: changes are gated behind a feature flag for staged rollout; legacy resources without kms metadata fall back to audit-only behavior until backfill completes. 5) Tests & CI: unit tests for evaluator, integration tests for end-to-end key-region enforcement, and e2e smoke for canary rollout. 6) Docs: updated RBAC v2 policy docs and platform migration guide to include KMS residency best practices. Rollout plan: enable the feature flag in a Canary region for 24-48 hours with elevated logging; run backfill job; if metrics stable (no unexpected denials), ramp to 50% across dedicated capacity pools, then full rollout. See linked Linear tickets for rollout milestones. Motivation, design, and alternatives are captured in ENG-4321. rollout_notes: Stage 1: Feature flag off by default. Deploy to main and run backfill in background (non-enforcing).
Stage 2: Enable feature flag in Canary region with 5% traffic for 24 hours. Monitor residency_denials, audit event volume, and error rates.
Stage 3: If metrics stable, ramp to 50% on Dedicated, run additional backfill passes. Coordinate with Private installer team for on-prem KMS metadata exposure.
Rollback: Disable feature flag; migration is backward-compatible and backfill is idempotent. Remove enforcement if unexpected user impact observed.
